pre_mortem: A strong solver reads SOP CB-3 end to end, lists the shipped departures (total counts, seed viability, running PDL per line in log order, thaw restarting at seed and +1 passage, flags on PDL with a 5-doubling band, vials not reduced by thaws, bank PDL from the latest freeze), writes its own reference from sections 2-6 and fuzzes the package against it.
Every departure is self-verifiable against that reference, so all nine will be repaired.

It goes wrong only where its own reference holds its opinion: (1) viable counts computed from a viability below 70.0, or a hybrid of viable harvest over total seed, instead of today's total-count figure; (2) a bank with no vial in stock reported as null or as the highest PDL ever frozen instead of today's latest-freeze figure.

Both traps are now bounded only by definitions (2.3 valid count, 2.5 bank in use) away from their rules, with one general value-level silence sentence; nothing names either case. The empty max() in T2 still raises in a solver's fuzz and sends it to the silence sentence, so T2 is the likelier collapse.
prediction: borderline; resists only if T1 (definition-bounded viable counts) or T2 bites
decisive_reason: departures remain explicit closed-form rules (reviewer is right there); the only lever is the two definition-bounded traps, now the shape that took candidate A from 2/2 to 1/2, so 3 and not higher.
